column1: # DoctKey acceptance fixtures — literal fallback (and smart off).
# Format: method,mode,smart,tone_style <TAB> keys <TAB> expected document text
# The smart fallback gives English back in three situations:
#   1. the keystrokes cannot be Vietnamese at all (`hello`, `google`);
#   2. a Telex tone key sits inside an English consonant cluster (`st`, `rt`,
#      `xt`, …), where it cannot be a Vietnamese operator (`best`, `first`);
#   3. the keystrokes are a known English collision whose Vietnamese reading is
#      not a common Vietnamese word (`this`, `does`, `door`; see
# Keystrokes that spell a common Vietnamese word stay Vietnamese.
# smart ON: words that cannot be Vietnamese fall back to the literal keystrokes
# smart ON: a final repeated operator must not eat a letter of an English word
# smart ON: a tone key inside an English consonant cluster stays a letter.
# `st`/`rt`/`xt`/`rk`/`rm` cannot occur in a Vietnamese syllable, so the tone
# mark is written after the word instead (`bets`, `lits`, `quets` below).
# ... and the same letters with the tone key typed last are still Vietnamese
# smart ON: known English collisions whose Vietnamese reading is obscure
# short, very frequent English words whose Vietnamese reading is obscure
# smart ON: Vietnamese-first still wins when the Vietnamese word is common.
# These are the same keys, but the Vietnamese reading is a real, frequent word,
# so it keeps its marks (`thees`/`theer`/`theem`/`reets` type the same words).
# short Vietnamese words are never taken by the English list
# smart ON: valid Vietnamese is kept (even if the keystrokes were accidental)
# smart OFF: the same keystrokes are always transformed
# VNI: an escaped word must not swallow following digits
